End-user sales and rentals still occur, but are executed **within our own circles or through partner brokers**; the marketing identity and client-facing focus remain **investor-forward at all times**. White-label partners carry **no such mandate** and may serve end users freely.
344	**Reason:** This is what makes the brand mean something. A brand that sells everything to everyone has no thesis; a brand with a clear investment thesis attracts a specific investor and a specific franchisee, and makes product selection objectively decidable rather than a matter of taste. 14	# BluePrint Product Constitution
15	
16	> **Decision authority:** This is the definitive product-boundary document for BluePrint. Product briefs, wireframes, roadmaps and implementation decisions must conform to it. A material change requires a dated entry in [[../00_Index/Decision Log|Decision Log]] and corresponding updates here, in [[Platform Information Architecture]], [[MVP Scope]], and in the ecosystem maps.
17	
18	## 1. Product promise
19	
20	**BluePrint gives a real-estate company a professional back office from day one.** It converts a qualified opportunity into a controlled, documented and financially visible transaction while coordinating the specialist systems the company already uses.
21	
22	Standalone promise:
23	
24	> Run the agency's back-office operation with clear responsibilities, compliant workflows, approved documents, commission control and reliable management information—even when the agency uses another CRM or no connected CRM.
25	
26	Ecosystem promise:
27	
28	> Connect the same BluePrint workspace to B_RealEstate's training, curated inventory, off-market marketplace, operating standards, benchmarks and shared services without changing the core product.
29	
30	The measurable outcome is not “everything in one place.” It is **fewer missed steps, faster document preparation, lower administrative effort, fewer commission errors, clearer accountability and more reliable closings**.
31	
32	## 2. Product category and boundary
33	
34	BluePrint is a **multi-tenant real-estate back-office operating platform and system of operational record**.
35	
36	It is:
37	
38	- The transaction workspace after a lead becomes operationally qualified.
39	- The control layer for compliance gates, documents, tasks, approvals and commissions.
40	- The structured operational memory of the agency.
41	- The management layer for back-office metrics and reporting.
42	- The governed interface through which the BluePrint Copilot reads company knowledge and prepares permitted work.
43	- Connector-neutral: it supports GoHighLevel, other CRMs and manual intake through the same domain model.
44	
45	It is not:
46	
47	- A lead-generation or marketing automation platform.
48	- A replacement for GoHighLevel or another CRM.
49	- A general-purpose chatbot.
50	- An LMS or course-delivery engine.
51	- An off-market marketplace.
52	- A file-storage replacement.
53	- An e-signature provider.
54	- A bank, payment rail, escrow provider or general ledger.
55	- A source of legal, tax, financial or investment advice.
56	- A promise that every ecosystem component shares one physical database.
57	
58	## 3. Product principles
59	
60	1. **Standalone first, ecosystem amplified.** Every agency receives a complete core workflow; B_RealEstate integrations add leverage rather than unlock basic operability.
61	2. **One operational spine.** All customers use the same transaction state model. CRM choice changes the intake adapter, not the product.
62	3. **One owner per fact.** Every important field has a declared system of record and synchronization direction.
63	4. **Structured data creates documents.** Approved templates and governed inputs generate documents; documents do not become the hidden database.
64	5. **Human accountability survives automation.** AI may explain, analyze, draft and prepare actions, but accountable people approve legal, compliance and financial consequences.
65	6. **Need-to-know by default.** Tenant isolation, role permissions and record-level access apply to users, integrations and AI alike.
66	7. **Explain before surprise.** Status, calculations, AI sources and blocked steps must be understandable.
67	8. **Exceptions are visible.** A bypass requires authority, reason and an audit event; it cannot silently erase a control.
68	9. **Integrate specialist tools; do not recreate them.** BluePrint stores references, status and evidence while the specialist platform performs its specialist job.
69	10. **Measure outcomes.** Features are justified by operational time saved, control improvement, transaction quality or revenue visibility.
70	
71	## 4. What BluePrint owns
72	
73	| Domain | BluePrint responsibility | Canonical record |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Tenant operations | Company workspace, market configuration, business line and operating settings | Tenant and workspace records |
76	| Identity authorization | BluePrint roles, permissions and record access; federated identity may come from an external identity provider | Role assignments and access policy |
77	| Opportunity handoff | Operational snapshot of a qualified opportunity and link to its originating CRM record | Intake record + external reference |
78	| Transaction | Stage, operational owner, requirements, deadlines, blockers, decision trail and outcome | Transaction workspace |
79	| Project/unit operations | Approved project/unit facts required to execute a transaction; provenance and external source retained | Project/unit operational master |
80	| Compliance workflow | Requirements, evidence status, reviews, exceptions and approval gates | Compliance check records |
81	| Template governance | Approved template, jurisdiction, use case, version, effective dates and required inputs | Template registry |
82	| Generated documents | Draft/final status, template lineage, input snapshot, approval and specialist-storage link | Document record and audit evidence |
83	| Work coordination | Tasks, owners, due dates, dependencies, escalation and completion evidence | Task and approval records |
84	| Commission control | Calculation basis, waterfall, expected/approved/paid status and reconciliation references | Commission statement |
85	| Operational reporting | BluePrint-derived KPIs, workflow health, close status and management reports | Metric definitions and report snapshots |
86	| Company knowledge | Indexed, permission-filtered references to approved manuals, policies, procedures and templates | Knowledge-source registry |
87	| AI activity | Request context, sources, draft/action, cost, confirmation and result | AI run and tool-action log |
88	| Audit | Who changed what, when, why, through which interface and under what authority | Immutable audit event |
89	
90	## 5. What external systems own
91	
92	| External system | It owns | BluePrint stores/uses |
93	|---|---|---|
94	| GoHighLevel or another CRM | Lead capture, marketing source, conversations, campaigns, nurturing, appointments and pre-handoff qualification | External ID, qualified snapshot, selected shared fields and operational status returned to CRM |
95	| Open edX | Course content, enrollment, learning activity, assessments and certificates | Identity link, relevant completion/certification status and expiry used for readiness gates |
96	| VAULTED | Off-market discovery, listing visibility, marketplace access and marketplace engagement | Listing reference and transaction created after an authorized handoff |
97	| Dproperty Select governance | HQ approval of curated inventory, controlled assumptions, commercial terms and approved materials | Approved project/unit reference and effective version used in a transaction |
98	| Drive/SharePoint or approved document store | Binary files and folder retention where policy assigns it | Stable file link, metadata, checksum/version reference and access status |
99	| E-signature provider | Signing ceremony, signer authentication and signature evidence | Envelope ID, status, signed-file reference and evidence link |
100	| Accounting/payment provider | Ledger, invoices, taxes, money movement, reconciliation and payment evidence | Expected amounts, external transaction/invoice IDs and reconciliation status |
101	| Identity provider | Authentication and identity proofing when configured | Tenant membership, application role and last verified identity reference |
102	
103	**Rule:** “Integrated” never means “duplicated without ownership.” The [[../18_Ecosystem/12 - System of Record and Integration Matrix|System of Record and Integration Matrix]] controls the wider ecosystem boundary.
104	
105	## 6. Three CRM operating modes
106	
107	All three modes create the same `Intake` and `Transaction` records and enter the same workflow.
108	
109	### Mode A — Ecosystem Connected
110	
111	**Customer:** Dproperty franchise or B_RealEstate partner using the configured GoHighLevel environment.
112	
113	- GoHighLevel owns lead capture, communication and qualification.
114	- A configured qualifying stage/event creates a BluePrint intake.
115	- BluePrint returns operational status, selected milestone and closing outcome.
116	- Identity may be federated for a unified experience.
117	- Ecosystem inventory, Academy and benchmark features may be enabled by entitlement.
118	
119	### Mode B — External CRM Connected
120	
121	**Customer:** Independent agency retaining its own CRM.
122	
123	- The customer's CRM remains the front-office source of truth.
124	- Intake arrives through the standard API/webhook contract or a supported connector.
125	- External IDs and field ownership prevent duplicate records and sync loops.
126	- Only the minimum authorized client/opportunity information is transferred.
127	- BluePrint returns operational milestones through the same integration contract where supported.
128	
129	### Mode C — BluePrint Direct
130	
131	**Customer:** Small/new agency without a connected CRM, or an agency operating temporarily without integration.
132	
133	- Authorized users create an intake through a guided form or CSV import.
134	- BluePrint stores only the operational contact/opportunity snapshot required for the transaction.
135	- BluePrint does not add campaign, bulk messaging or nurture functionality.
136	- The same workflow begins after validation; no “lite” transaction model is created.
137	
138	### Connector contract
139	
140	Every intake records:
141	
142	- `tenant_id`
143	- `intake_id`
144	- `source_mode`
145	- `external_system`
146	- `external_record_id`
147	- `external_record_url`
148	- `source_event_id` or import batch
149	- `received_at`
150	- `last_synced_at`
151	- field ownership map
152	- consent/privacy flags received from the source
153	- idempotency key
154	- processing and error state
155	
156	Repeated events must update or reject safely; they must not create duplicate transactions.
157	
158	## 7. Core data entities
159	
160	| Domain | Core entities | Purpose |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| Tenancy and security | Tenant, Workspace, Market, User, Role, Permission, Membership | Isolation and authorized access |
163	| Parties | Person, Organization, Party Role, Contact Reference | Transaction participants without recreating CRM marketing history |
164	| Intake | Intake, Source Reference, Qualification Snapshot, Assignment | Normalize CRM/manual entry |
165	| Transaction | Transaction, Stage, Milestone, Activity, Exception, Outcome | Operational spine |
166	| Inventory | Project, Unit, Listing Reference, Availability Snapshot, Commercial Term Version | Transaction-ready property context |
167	| Compliance | Requirement, Check, Evidence, Review, Decision, Exception | Gate progression and prove control |
168	| Documents | Template, Template Version, Data Schema, Document, File Reference, Signature Envelope | Govern creation and lifecycle |
169	| Work | Task, Checklist, Dependency, Approval, Escalation, SLA | Coordinate people and controls |
170	| Finance | Commission Rule, Calculation, Statement, Payout Allocation, Invoice Reference, Reconciliation | Make economics visible and auditable |
171	| Knowledge | Knowledge Source, Procedure, Policy, Manual Section, Effective Version | Ground users and Copilot |
172	| Reporting | Metric Definition, Metric Value, Report, Snapshot, Benchmark Cohort | Reproducible management information |
173	| Integration | Connection, Mapping, Sync Event, Webhook Event, Error, Retry | Connector-neutral interoperability |
174	| AI and audit | Conversation, AI Run, Citation, Proposed Action, Confirmation, Audit Event | Safe assistance and traceability |
175	
176	Every tenant-owned entity carries, at minimum, a stable ID, `tenant_id`, creation/update timestamps, actor/provenance, lifecycle status and access classification. Sensitive entities also carry retention and jurisdiction attributes.
177	
178	## 8. Canonical transaction state model
179	
180	```mermaid
181	stateDiagram-v2
182	    [*] --> IntakeReceived
183	    IntakeReceived --> IntakeValidated
184	    IntakeValidated --> WorkspaceOpen
185	    WorkspaceOpen --> CompliancePending
186	    CompliancePending --> DocumentPreparation: requirements satisfied
187	    DocumentPreparation --> ApprovalPending
188	    ApprovalPending --> SignatureOrReservation: approved
189	    SignatureOrReservation --> ClosingPending
190	    ClosingPending --> ClosedWon
191	    ClosingPending --> ClosedLost
192	    ClosingPending --> Cancelled
193	    ClosedWon --> CommissionPending
194	    CommissionPending --> CommissionApproved
195	    CommissionApproved --> CommissionPaid
196	    CommissionPaid --> ReportedAndArchived
197	```
198	
199	Stages are stable across customers. Market, business-line and tenant configurations determine the requirements, templates, roles, calculations and approvals inside a stage.
200	
201	## 9. MVP boundary
202	
203	### Included in MVP
204	
205	1. Multi-tenant workspaces, authentication, roles and record-level access foundation.
206	2. Intake through configured GoHighLevel handoff, standard webhook/API, guided manual entry and CSV import.
207	3. Intake validation, duplicate protection and external-source references.
208	4. Transaction workspace with stage, participants, project/unit, next action, timeline, blockers and audit trail.
209	5. Configurable compliance checklist with evidence, review and approval gates.
210	6. Governed template registry and generation of a deliberately small approved document set.
211	7. Tasks, checklists, approvals, due dates and escalation.
212	8. E-signature handoff and returned status/reference; no proprietary signature engine.
213	9. Deterministic commission calculation, review and payout status for approved MVP rules.
214	10. Operational dashboard and weekly transaction/commission report.
215	11. Searchable company knowledge registry and BluePrint Copilot MVP.
216	12. Integration administration, sync-event log and recoverable error queue.
217	13. Immutable security/operational audit events for consequential activity.
218	
219	### Explicitly outside MVP
220	
221	- Marketing automation, bulk messaging, call tracking or lead nurture.
222	- A full accounting, invoicing, tax, banking, escrow or payment product.
223	- Course authoring/delivery.
224	- VAULTED marketplace browsing/negotiation implementation.
225	- Full Dproperty Select curation workflow beyond approved-data consumption.
226	- Native file-storage or e-signature infrastructure.
227	- Advanced AI autonomy, unsupervised external communication or automatic legal/compliance approval.
228	- Cross-tenant benchmarking until privacy thresholds and metric consistency are proven.
229	- General-purpose custom workflow builder.
230	- Client portal, developer portal and mobile-native applications unless required by the pilot.
231	- Complex multi-market localization beyond the first approved market pack.
232	
233	### MVP wedge
234	
235	The MVP succeeds when all three CRM modes can complete one golden workflow without separate product variants:
236	
237	**qualified opportunity → transaction workspace → compliance → document generation → approval → closing → commission → report**.
238	
239	The canonical wireframe and architecture test are in [[BluePrint Golden Workflow - Wireframe and Validation]].
240	
241	## 10. BluePrint Copilot constitution
242	
243	### Promise
244	
245	The Copilot is a permission-aware operational assistant that understands BluePrint, the user's company configuration, authorized company knowledge and the current record. It helps the user find, understand, summarize, draft and prepare work inside the product.
246	
247	It is not an open-ended ChatGPT replacement. It must stay within BluePrint's supported domains and state when a request is outside its authority or evidence.
248	
249	### Permission levels
250	
251	| Level | Capability | MVP behavior | Examples |
252	|---|---|---|---|
253	| AI-0 — Explain and retrieve | Read authorized product/company knowledge | Execute immediately; cite sources | “How do I register a reservation?” “Find the approved NDA.” |
254	| AI-1 — Summarize and analyze | Read authorized records and compute through approved tools | Execute immediately; show sources, period and definitions | Transaction summary, missing-items list, KPI explanation |
255	| AI-2 — Draft | Create non-final content from approved templates and structured inputs | Save as draft; show template/version and missing inputs | NDA draft, weekly report, task checklist |
256	| AI-3 — Prepare an action | Assemble a proposed change or external handoff | Preview impact; require explicit user confirmation; log result | Create tasks, update non-restricted status, prepare e-signature envelope |
257	| AI-4 — Restricted authority | Approve, sign, pay, publish, waive controls or make regulated decisions | **AI prohibited. Human role performs the decision.** | Compliance approval, contract signature, payment release, commission approval, template publication |
258	
259	Tenant and role permissions always override the general AI level. The Copilot cannot retrieve or act on a record the requesting user cannot access directly.
260	
261	### Mandatory guardrails
262	
263	- Tenant isolation at retrieval, prompt construction, tool execution, caches and logs.
264	- Need-to-know record filtering before model invocation.
265	- Sources/citations for company knowledge, policy, procedure and KPI answers.
266	- No invented field values. Missing required inputs are requested explicitly.
267	- Template and template-version provenance on every generated document.
268	- Deterministic services—not model arithmetic—for commissions, projections and KPI calculations.
269	- Human approval for legal, compliance, financial, signature and external-communication consequences.
270	- Full audit of prompt category, sources, model, tools, output, confirmation and cost; sensitive raw content retained only under approved policy.
271	- Clear uncertainty and refusal when evidence is missing, conflicting, expired or unauthorized.
272	- No learning across tenants from customer content without an explicit, legally approved program.
273	
274	### AI economics
275	
276	BluePrint owns the Copilot experience, knowledge architecture, permissions, evaluation suite, tools, routing and cost policy while using approved foundation-model APIs.
277	
278	- Include a defined monthly AI allowance by subscription tier.
279	- Meter usage by tenant and capability.
280	- Route retrieval/classification and simple summaries to cost-efficient models.
281	- Use stronger models only for approved complex drafting/analysis.
282	- Use deterministic code for calculations and rules.
283	- Cache reusable non-sensitive results where safe.
284	- Alert and throttle before a tenant exceeds its allowance; offer priced overage rather than silent margin erosion.
285	
286	Pricing amounts remain controlled by the financial model and [[../18_Ecosystem/14 - Unit Economics Registry|Unit Economics Registry]].
287	
288	## 11. Standalone versus ecosystem capabilities
289	
290	| Capability | BluePrint standalone | With B_RealEstate ecosystem |
291	|---|---|---|
292	| Transaction workflow | Full | Full, with ecosystem configurations |
293	| CRM | Any supported external CRM or direct intake | Preconfigured GoHighLevel handoff and status return |
294	| Documents | Customer's approved templates | B_RealEstate/Dproperty template packs subject to entitlement and localization |
295	| Compliance | Customer-configured/approved requirements | Market packs, operating standards and HQ oversight where contracted |
296	| Knowledge and SOPs | Customer's materials | B_RealEstate manuals, playbooks and shared-service guidance |
297	| Academy | Links or external certification reference | Open edX provisioning and certification/readiness gates |
298	| Inventory | Customer's project/unit records and external references | Dproperty Select approved inventory and VAULTED handoffs where entitled |
299	| Reporting | Tenant operational and financial-control metrics | Network-standard definitions and later privacy-safe benchmarks |
300	| Support | Product support | Product support plus contracted launch/coaching/shared services |
301	| Copilot | Customer knowledge + BluePrint help + tenant records | Adds authorized ecosystem manuals, inventory context and operating rules |
302	
303	No standalone customer must join Dproperty, adopt GoHighLevel, use VAULTED or consume B_RealEstate inventory to obtain the core workflow.
304	
305	## 12. Product shell
306	
307	The default navigation is:
308	
309	1. Home
310	2. Transactions
311	3. Projects & Inventory
312	4. Documents
313	5. Tasks & Approvals
314	6. Finance
315	7. Reports
316	8. Knowledge
317	9. Integrations
318	10. Administration
319	
320	The Copilot is available through a global command entry and a context panel on supported records. The interface opens on **what requires attention**, not on every available module.
321	
322	## 13. Non-functional release gates
323	
324	- No cross-tenant data path in automated security tests.
325	- Role and record-level authorization enforced server-side for UI, API, exports and AI tools.
326	- Audit event for every restricted data change, approval and external handoff.
327	- Retry-safe and idempotent integration events.
328	- Time-zone, currency and jurisdiction attributes are explicit; no hidden tenant-wide assumption where a transaction can differ.
329	- Accessibility baseline for keyboard navigation, form labels, focus, contrast and reduced motion.
330	- Exportability of tenant-owned operational data and documented retention/deletion controls.
331	- Backups, recovery objectives and incident response defined before production use.
332	- Model/provider substitution possible without rewriting product permissions or domain services.
333	
334	## 14. MVP success measures
335	
336	The pilot baseline must be recorded before targets are finalized. At minimum, measure:
337	
338	- Time from qualified handoff to transaction workspace.
339	- Duplicate-entry rate and synchronization failures.
340	- Percentage of transactions with complete required evidence at each gate.
341	- Document preparation and approval cycle time.
342	- Overdue operational tasks and exceptions.
343	- Commission calculation/reconciliation errors.
344	- Time required to produce the weekly management report.
345	- Copilot answer traceability, document-draft acceptance, user corrections and cost per successful task.
346	- User-reported confidence: “I know what needs attention and why.”
347	
348	## 15. Change control
349	
350	A proposal changes this Constitution when it alters the product promise, source-of-truth ownership, canonical state model, CRM modes, MVP boundary, AI authority or standalone entitlement.
351	
352	For such a change:
353	
354	1. State the operational problem and evidence.
355	2. Identify the Constitution clause affected.
356	3. Analyze impacts on all three CRM modes.
357	4. Analyze security, legal, financial, integration and AI consequences.
358	5. Record the approved decision and effective version.
359	6. Update dependent maps, specifications, tests, public claims and contracts together.
360	
361	Implementation details that do not change these boundaries may evolve through normal product design.

14	# BluePrint Golden Workflow — Wireframe and Validation

17	
18	> **Controlling document:** [[BluePrint Product Constitution]]. If a screen or scenario conflicts with the Constitution, the Constitution wins until a formal change decision is recorded.

20	## 1. Validation question
21	
22	Can one product—with configuration and intake adapters, not separate codebases—take all three customers through the same operational journey?
23	
24	1. Independent agency using its own CRM.
25	2. Dproperty franchise using GoHighLevel.
26	3. Small agency using BluePrint manually.
27	
28	Required journey:
29	
30	**CRM/manual intake → transaction workspace → compliance → document generation → approval → closing → commission → report**
31	
32	The Copilot must provide useful assistance at every stage without gaining legal, compliance, signature, payment or final-approval authority.
33	
34	## 2. Golden-workflow invariants
35	
36	These rules do not change by tenant or CRM mode:
37	
38	- One normalized Intake enters BluePrint.
39	- One validated Intake creates or links to one Transaction.
40	- One Transaction has one current stage, one accountable operational owner and visible next action.
41	- Stage progress is controlled by configured requirements, not by hidden UI logic.
42	- Documents are generated from approved versioned templates and structured data.
43	- Consequential decisions are performed by authorized humans.
44	- Commission outputs come from deterministic rules and require review/approval.
45	- Reports use governed metric definitions and a dated snapshot.
46	- Every important change produces an audit event.
47	- The Copilot sees only the data the requesting user is authorized to see.
48	
49	## 3. Workflow and states
50	
51	```mermaid
52	flowchart TD
53	    A["1. Intake received"] --> B["2. Intake validated"]
54	    B --> C["3. Transaction workspace"]
55	    C --> D["4. Compliance gate"]
56	    D --> E["5. Documents generated"]
57	    E --> F["6. Human approval and signature handoff"]
58	    F --> G["7. Closing recorded"]
59	    G --> H["8. Commission controlled"]
60	    H --> I["9. Reported and archived"]
61	```

64	|---|---|---|---|
65	| Intake received | Source event/manual submission accepted | Required intake fields and duplicate checks reviewed | Operations Coordinator |
66	| Intake validated | Valid source, party and opportunity snapshot | Existing/new transaction decision recorded | Operations Coordinator |
67	| Transaction workspace | Transaction created with owner and next action | Required parties/project/unit/workflow configuration selected | Transaction owner |
68	| Compliance gate | Applicable requirements instantiated | Required evidence approved or authorized exception recorded | Compliance reviewer |
69	| Documents generated | Data schema and approved template available | Complete draft package generated and reviewed for missing data | Document preparer |
70	| Approval/signature | Draft package ready | Required internal approvals complete and e-signature/external execution initiated | Authorized approver |

72	| Commission | Closed-won economics available | Calculation approved and payout/reconciliation status recorded | Finance approver |

228	## 9. Desk-test fixtures

305	## 11. Architecture-test verdict
306	
307	**Result: PASS at product-architecture level.** All three scenarios complete the same canonical workflow, state model, core entities, screens and Copilot permission contract.

312	- External-system references and outbound milestones.
313	- Tenant brand and approved templates.

315	- Commission rule version.
316	- Ecosystem entitlements and data sources.

322	## 12. Exceptions and failure-state tests
323	
324	| Failure/exception | Required product behavior | Copilot role |
325	|---|---|---|
326	| Duplicate source event | Do not create a second Intake/Transaction; show linked result | Explain idempotency result |
327	| Possible duplicate party/opportunity | Hold for authorized review | Summarize candidate similarities; never merge autonomously |
328	| CRM unavailable | Queue/retry inbound or outbound event; show sync age/error | Explain failure and safe next action |
329	| Missing required intake data | Block transaction creation or mark incomplete according to configuration | List missing fields and draft correction request |
330	| Conflicting CRM/BluePrint value | Apply field ownership rule; show conflict | Explain owner/provenance; prepare proposed correction |
331	| Expired/insufficient compliance evidence | Block affected progression | Cite requirement and request new evidence |
332	| User lacks access to evidence | Hide content and actions server-side | State lack of permission without revealing content |
333	| Template expired/not approved | Prevent generation | Locate approved alternative or escalate |
334	| AI cannot ground answer | Refuse to invent; show missing/conflicting sources | Ask for clarification or direct user to owner |
335	| E-signature provider unavailable | Preserve approved package; queue/retry handoff or allow authorized external-reference workflow | Explain status; never claim sent/signed |
336	| Closing facts differ from expected | Require confirmation and preserve variance | Summarize variance; do not overwrite silently |
337	| Commission rule missing/conflicting | Block statement approval | Identify missing rule; no free-form calculation |
338	| Report source corrected after issuance | Create corrected version; retain prior snapshot | Explain changes and affected KPIs |

340	## 13. MVP prototype acceptance criteria

353	- [ ] Every transaction shows owner, next action, blocker and audit history.
354	- [ ] Templates, requirements and commission rules are effective-dated/versioned.
355	- [ ] Closing, commission and report values can be traced to source fields and rules.
356	- [ ] Exceptions require reason, authority and an audit event.
357	
358	### Copilot
359	
360	- [ ] Retrieval respects tenant, role and record access before model invocation.
361	- [ ] Company/process answers cite authorized sources.
362	- [ ] Document drafts identify template/version and missing inputs.
363	- [ ] Metrics and commissions come from governed services, not model arithmetic.
364	- [ ] AI-3 actions show a preview and require confirmation.
365	- [ ] AI cannot perform AI-4 decisions/actions.
366	- [ ] AI run, tools, sources, confirmation, output status and cost are auditable.
367	
368	### Usability
369	
370	- [ ] A new user can identify what needs attention from Home.
371	- [ ] Each stage has one clear primary action.
372	- [ ] Keyboard, focus, labels, errors and reduced-motion behavior meet the agreed accessibility baseline.
373	- [ ] The same scenario can be demonstrated without hidden administrator intervention.

390	| `/integrations` | Connections and event log | CRM/provider configuration and errors |
391	| `/admin` | Tenant, roles and workflow configuration | Authorized configuration only |
392	
393	The Copilot is a panel/command surface within these routes, not a separate general-chat destination.
394	
395	## 15. Prototype build order
396	
397	1. Application shell, tenancy, roles and audit primitives.
398	2. Canonical Intake schema, manual form and Intake Inbox.
399	3. Transaction Overview and state/requirements engine.

12	# BluePrint Product Vision
13	
14	> Start in [[BluePrint Product Map]]. The binding definition is [[BluePrint Product Constitution]].
15	
16	BluePrint gives a real-estate company a professional back office from day one. It converts qualified opportunities into controlled, documented and financially visible transactions while coordinating—not replacing—the CRM, storage, e-signature, accounting, Academy and marketplace systems around it.
17	
18	## Product principles
19	
20	- Standalone first; ecosystem amplified.
21	- One transaction spine for GoHighLevel, another CRM or BluePrint Direct.
22	- One owner per fact.
23	- Structured data creates documents.
24	- Deterministic rules control calculations and gates.
25	- Human accountability survives automation.
26	- Need-to-know permissions apply to people, integrations and the Copilot.
27	- Exceptions remain visible and auditable.
28	- Measure operational outcomes, not module count.

31	
32	BluePrint should feel premium, calm, structured and boutique rather than corporate. It opens on what requires attention, explains what happens next and keeps evidence close to every decision.

36	## MVP goal
37

12	
13	# Roles and Access Matrix
14	
15	> **Precedence update (2026-08-16):** Role names remain abstract/configurable. Need-to-know access and AI-0–AI-4 authority are controlled by [[BluePrint Product Constitution]]; Golden Workflow actors and separation rules are in [[BluePrint Golden Workflow - Wireframe and Validation]].
16	
17	
18	> Defines the platform hierarchy, the minimum roles a franchise office must have, where the Copilot may support human roles, the confidentiality rules, and how AI usage is priced into the plan. Companion to [[Platform Information Architecture]] and [[Platform Scenario Playbook]].
19	>
20	> **Key insight:** the roles defined here become BOTH the permission tiers in the software AND the minimum staffing requirement in the franchise agreement.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Hierarchy
25	
26	```
27	HQ (Dproperty)
28	├── HQ Admin / Super Admin ........... everything, all tenants
29	├── HQ Legal / Compliance ............ approves templates, clauses, signed docs
30	├── HQ Finance ....................... royalties, network fees, splits
31	└── HQ Private Collection Manager .... curates & assigns curated inventory
32	        │
33	        ▼  (each franchise is a tenant)
34	FRANCHISE OFFICE
35	├── Franchise Principal / Owner ...... 1 required — accountable, legal signatory
36	├── Sales Manager .................... optional early (Principal can wear this hat)
37	├── Sales Advisor / Agent ............ 1+ required — client-facing, closes deals
38	├── Operations / Admin Coordinator ... 1 required — documents, compliance, data hygiene
39	└── Marketing Lead ................... optional (can be AI + GHL)
40	```
41	
42	**Minimum viable franchise office = 3 humans:** Principal + one Sales Advisor + one Operations Coordinator. Everything else starts as AI + HQ-shared services and is added as the office grows.
43	
44	> Franchise-agreement line: *"To operate a Dproperty franchise you must maintain at minimum a Principal, a licensed Sales Advisor, and an Operations Coordinator."*
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Role → access summary (what each role sees)
49	
50	| Role | Sees | Cannot see |
51	|------|------|-----------|
52	| HQ Admin | All tenants, all modules, all dashboards | — |
53	| HQ Legal/Compliance | Templates, clauses, signed docs, cases (compliance), audit log | Personal HR grievances unrelated to compliance |
54	| HQ Finance | Royalties, splits, invoices, payouts across network | HR grievances |
55	| HQ Private Collection Mgr | Curated inventory, authorized franchises, PC deals | Unrelated franchise internal data |
56	| Franchise Principal | Own tenant: team, clients, brokers, deals, finance, reporting, PC (approved) | Other tenants; HR grievances *about themselves* |
57	| Sales Manager | Team pipeline, team performance, own-tenant reporting | HQ-wide data, other tenants |
58	| Sales Advisor | Assigned clients, deals, tasks, docs, projections | Other advisors' private clients (unless shared), finance internals |
59	| Operations Coordinator | Documents, compliance checklist, data hygiene, back-office | Commission internals (unless granted) |
60	| Marketing Lead | CRM & Marketing, campaigns, public-site leads | Deal financials |
61	
62	**Confidentiality is a property of the *case/record*, not a separate app.** An HR grievance about a Principal must hide from that Principal — visibility rules live at the record level. Build once, reuse everywhere.
63	
64	---
65	
66	## Human roles and AI support map
67	
68	| Role / Function | Human or AI | Notes |
69	|---|---|---|
70	| Franchise Principal | **Human** | Accountability, legal signatory |
71	| Sales Advisor (closing) | **Human** | Relationship + legal duty; AI assists, doesn't replace |
72	| Ops / Compliance sign-off | **Human** | Final checks, heavily AI-assisted |
73	| SDR / lead qualifier | **GoHighLevel automation / human** | Front-office function outside the BluePrint Copilot; qualified handoff enters BluePrint |
74	| Nurture / follow-up | **GoHighLevel automation / human** | Front-office function outside the BluePrint Copilot |
75	| Document drafting support | **Copilot AI-2** | Uses approved versioned templates and structured inputs; output remains draft |
76	| Projection support | **Deterministic service + Copilot AI-1/2** | Service calculates; Copilot explains or drafts narrative; human approves where required |
77	| Meeting/transaction summarizer | **Copilot AI-1/3** | Summarizes immediately; proposed record actions require confirmation |
78	| Reporting support | **Deterministic metrics + Copilot AI-1/2** | Metrics are governed; Copilot explains and drafts narrative |
79	| Knowledge/training support | **Copilot AI-0/1** | Answers from authorized BluePrint/company/Academy sources with citations |
80	| Receipt/evidence extraction | **Copilot AI-1** | Extraction only; human validates and approves financial action |
81	| Ticket/glitch assistance | **Rules + Copilot AI-1/3** | Rules route; Copilot summarizes/clusters or prepares confirmed changes; humans resolve |
82	
83	**The pattern:** deterministic services calculate, gate, file and route; the Copilot retrieves, explains, summarizes, drafts and prepares confirmed low-risk actions. Authorized humans approve, sign, pay, publish templates, waive controls and make regulated decisions. See [[BluePrint Product Constitution]] §10.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Human vs AI — required-approval actions (always human + audit-logged)
88	- Approving payments, reimbursements, refunds
89	- Resolving disputes / grievances
90	- Final compliance / legal sign-off
91	- Hiring / firing
92	- Deleting data / data-governance actions
93	- Signing contracts
94	
95	---
96	
97	## How Copilot usage is priced into the plan
98	
99	Three models — recommended hybrid:
100	
101	1. **Seats + bundled agents (base):** each plan tier includes always-on agents (SDR, Nurture, Doc drafter). Priced into the monthly franchise/software fee. Simple, predictable.
102	2. **Agent add-ons:** premium agents (advanced analyst, custom sales coach) sold as monthly upsells.
103	3. **Usage/credit-based:** monthly AI credit pool; overage billed. Protects margin.
104	
105	**Recommendation:** Base plan includes **2–3 core agents** (positioned as "a virtual team member included — worth one salary, included in your license"), premium agents as add-ons, and a **credit cap** to protect margin.
106	
107	Most workflow remains deterministic. Copilot usage runs through cost-aware approved GPT routing, tenant allowances and priced overage, so assistance can increase product value without silently eroding margin. See [[BluePrint Product Constitution]] §10 and the financial model.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Open items (see [[Open Questions]])
112	- Final default agent bundle per plan tier
113	- Credit cap sizing to protect margin
114	- Whether Sales Manager is required above N advisors
115	- LMS choice (LearnWorlds vs edX) affects Academy role provisioning

13	# Platform Information Architecture
14	
15	> **Naming and scope update (2026-08-16):** The platform is **BluePrint**, part of **B_RealEstate**. GoHighLevel remains the CRM, Open edX the Academy technology, and VAULTED the off-market marketplace. The canonical boundaries live in [[../18_Ecosystem/00 - Ecosystem Master Map]] and [[../18_Ecosystem/12 - System of Record and Integration Matrix]].
16	
17	> **Precedence update (2026-08-16):** [[BluePrint Product Constitution]] controls the product boundary and [[BluePrint Golden Workflow - Wireframe and Validation]] controls the MVP journey. This file remains supporting information architecture for the wider public/logged-in ecosystem.
18	>
19	> Companion notes: [[BluePrint Product Map]], [[Platform Scenario Playbook]] (72+ scenarios), and [[Roles and Access Matrix]] (hierarchy and permissions).
20	
21	---
22	
23	## The two design principles (these drive every decision)
24	
25	### Principle 1 — "Three clicks to anything" (the North Star)
26	One login. A persistent **Command Bar** (top of every screen) + a **Launcher grid** (home). Type or click → land on the file, contact, price, projection, template, brochure, external site, or CRM record. External links are fine **as long as they open from inside the OS** and feel like one ecosystem (SSO, no re-login).
27	
28	> If you work with us, you log into our site and within a few clicks you reach anything in our ecosystem — files, contacts, websites, information, prices, projections, templates, anything.
29	
30	### Principle 2 — Deterministic core, governed Copilot
31	
32	BluePrint includes the Copilot from MVP, but it does not turn deterministic workflow into probabilistic workflow. Route each task to the lowest-cost reliable mechanism:
33	
34	| Tier | Mechanism | Handles |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| **T0 — Deterministic** | Forms, rules, search index, templates, workflow services and calculations | Filing/routing, stage gates, document assembly, commissions, dashboards and audit |
37	| **T1 — Cost-efficient GPT** | Permission-filtered retrieval, classification, extraction and summaries | Q&A over approved knowledge, transaction summaries, missing-item explanations |
38	| **T2 — Stronger GPT** | Controlled complex drafting/analysis | Approved-template document drafts and management narratives |
39	
40	**Hard rules:**
41	
42	- Deterministic rules own filing, routing, calculations, stage gates and audit.
43	- AI may prepare a low-risk record action only with preview, explicit confirmation and authorization.
44	- AI never approves, signs, pays, publishes templates, waives controls or makes regulated decisions.
45	- Tenant/role/record permissions are enforced before retrieval and tool execution.
46	- Company/process/metric answers cite sources, definitions and period.
47	
48	See [[BluePrint Product Constitution]] §10 and [[AI Layer Notes]].
49	
50	---
51	
52	## The core architecture: two layers, one door
53	
54	```
55	LAYER 1 — PUBLIC SITE (no login)   → storefront / brand / recruitment
56	LAYER 2 — THE OS (after login)     → operating platform, role-gated
57	        └ single login link for everyone in a franchise office
58	        └ what you SEE is filtered by your ROLE, not by a different URL
59	```
60	
61	Everyone in a franchisee's office uses **one login link**. Role decides what loads (see [[Roles and Access Matrix]]).
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Layer 1 — Public site (pre-login): ~14 pages
66	
67	### Main public site (~8 pages)
68	| # | Page | Purpose |
69	|---|------|---------|
70	| 1 | Home | Positioning, hero, proof, dual CTA (client vs franchise) |
71	| 2 | About Us / Who We Are | Story, team, mission & vision |
72	| 3 | Services | Buyers, sellers, investors, developers |
73	| 4 | Private Collection (teaser) | Curated inventory, gated — "request access" |
74	| 5 | Projects / Listings (optional) | Public catalog, feeds leads into CRM |
75	| 6 | Contact / Book a call | Routes into GoHighLevel |
76	| 7 | Login / Portal entry | Door to Layer 2 |
77	| 8 | Legal | Privacy, terms, disclaimers |
78	
79	### "Become a Franchise" recruitment hub (~7 pages) — the growth engine
80	| # | Page | Purpose |
81	|---|------|---------|
82	| 1 | Why Dproperty | Value proposition (OS + CRM + Academy + brand + AI team included) |
83	| 2 | Your Path (Roadmap) | Discover → Apply → Sign → Onboard → Launch timeline |
84	| 3 | Investment & Returns | Fees, what's included, sample unit economics |
85	| 4 | What's Included | Platform, CRM, academy, brand, support, AI agents |
86	| 5 | Territories | Map of available/taken |
87	| 6 | Proof | Case studies, testimonials, numbers |
88	| 7 | FAQ | Financing, risk, timeline, exclusivity |
89	
90	Every recruitment page carries **Book a Call** + **Download Info Pack** (email-gated → drops into CRM nurture).
91	
92	**Two separate CRM pipelines:** *property buyers* vs *franchise prospects*. Never mix them.
93	**Prep Pack automation:** booking a call auto-sends agenda + info pack + short video (conversion multiplier).
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Layer 2 — The OS (post-login): ~25 modules
98	
99	### Two always-on top-bar elements (on every screen)
100	1. **Command Bar** — universal search + command palette (the "three clicks to anything").
101	2. **Report a Glitch** — one-click, no-blame improvement reporting (see Glitch system below).
102	
103	### Core operating modules (from [[Prototype Spec]] + additions)
104	HQ Control Center · Franchise Workspace Home · Clients · Brokers · Developers · Projects · Units · Deals · Document Generator · Projection Generator · Private Collection · Developer Sales Dashboard · Finance / Commission · Settings / Permissions
105	
106	### Modules added by this session
107	- **Resource Library** — templates, brochures, brand assets (surfaced from Drive, **not re-hosted**)
108	- **Learning / Academy** — embedded LMS (Open edX), SSO, gated certifications
109	- **CRM & Marketing** — embedded, white-labeled GoHighLevel, SSO
110	- **AI Assistant** — the T1 agent layer
111	- **Support / Help Desk** — tickets to HQ, knowledge base
112	- **Field Mode (mobile)** — stripped in-meeting/offline view (inventory, prices, media, contacts, NDA generator)
113	- **Franchise Sales Room** (HQ role) — full pitch package in one place for closing franchises
114	- **Data Room generator** — per-prospect shareable personalized microsite
115	
116	### Six back-office systems
117	| System | Purpose |
118	|--------|---------|
119	| **Finance / Back Office** | Commissions, royalties, invoices, payments, reimbursements, refunds, reconciliation, close. OS records; payment provider moves money. |
120	| **People / HR** | Users, roles, contracts, leave, payslips, reviews, on/offboarding, self-service "My Profile" |
121	| **Cases / Ticketing** | One engine for complaints, grievances, claims, disputes, escalations, whistleblower. **Case type controls visibility + routing + SLA.** |
122	| **Tenant Lifecycle** (in HQ Control Center) | Provision → audit → wind-down a franchise |
123	| **Audit Log & Data Governance** | Immutable trail, data requests, security flags |
124	| **Glitch Report** | No-blame, transparent, fast continuous-improvement reporting (Four Seasons model) |
125	
126	---
127	
128	## Embedding strategy: CRM & Academy (hybrid — embed + SSO)
129	
130	| System | Recommendation | Why |
131	|--------|---------------|-----|
132	| **GoHighLevel (CRM)** | White-label + embed via iframe/SSO inside "CRM & Marketing" | GHL is built for white-label reselling; franchisee never sees "GoHighLevel" |
133	| **Open edX (Academy)** | White-label + SSO, embed course player; deep-link for full LMS | Selected Academy engine. Onboarding should feel native and certifications must gate relevant BluePrint permissions/workflows. |
134	
135	**Single sign-on is the glue.** One login to the OS carries into CRM and Academy without re-auth. The OS is the **hub/launcher**; GoHighLevel and Open edX are **connected engines behind it**.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## File storage: stored in Drive, accessed through the OS (never duplicated)
140	
141	Extends [[File Storage Rules]]. The OS is the single pane of glass.
142	
143	| Thing | Stored in | Surfaced in OS as |
144	|-------|-----------|-------------------|
145	| Blank templates (contracts, NDAs) | Template Control (governed) | Document Generator pulls them |
146	| Brochures / brand assets / decks | SharePoint/Drive | Resource Library (links + preview) |
147	| Signed / legal documents | Secure legal archive | Linked from the Deal, read-only |
148	| Generated docs & projections | OS document store | Attached to the Deal |
149	| Structured operational data (party references, units, transactions) | BluePrint database | Source of truth only for BluePrint-owned fields; CRM-owned fields retain provenance |
150	
151	---
152	
153	## The Glitch Report system (Four Seasons model)
154	
155	Separate from the Cases engine — different tone, visibility, and goal.
156	
157	| | Cases engine | Glitch Report |
158	|---|---|---|
159	| Trigger | Something went wrong for a person; needs resolution | Anyone notices anything imperfect |
160	| Tone | Formal, accountable, SLA-bound | No-blame, low-friction, "help us improve" |
161	| Visibility | Confidential, role-gated | Transparent — visible to everyone |
162	| Goal | Resolve the case | Spot patterns → continuously improve |
163	
164	**Design:**
165	- Persistent **"Report a Glitch"** button on every screen + Field Mode.
166	- Near-zero friction: one line + auto-captured context (page, module, role, tenant, timestamp) + optional screenshot + severity mood (🟢/🟡/🔴).
167	- Two light tags: **Product glitch** (bug/UX) or **Experience glitch** (service/operation).
168	- **Glitch Feed:** network-wide live board of reported → in-progress → fixed (✅ + one-line "what we changed").
169	- **No-blame at the schema level:** glitches are never person-attributed.
170	- **AI (T1 only):** auto-categorize, de-duplicate/cluster, weekly "top 5 recurring" summary. Never resolves.
171	- Feeds HQ's improvement backlog → the loop that makes the ecosystem compound in quality.
172	
173	---
174	
175	## Franchisee lifecycle → login state
176	
177	```
178	DISCOVER → APPLY → SIGN → ONBOARD → LAUNCH → OPERATE → GROW
179	```
180	- **Discover / Apply** = public site (Layer 1)
181	- **Sign** = legal archive
182	- **Onboard → Grow** = inside the OS (Layer 2), role-gated
183	
184	---
185	
186	## System count (current)
187	- **~14 public pages** (8 main + 7 recruitment hub, minus shared)
188	- **~25 OS modules**
189	- **6 back-office systems:** Finance, People/HR, Cases, Tenant Lifecycle, Audit/Data Governance, Glitch Report
190	- **2 always-on top-bar elements:** Command Bar + Report a Glitch
191	
192	---
193	
194	## Next steps
195	1. ✅ Save architecture (this note + [[Platform Scenario Playbook]] + [[Roles and Access Matrix]])
196	2. Wireframe priority screens first (Public Home, Franchise Workspace Home, Deal Detail, Resource Library, Command Bar, Glitch Report) — not all 25 at once
197	3. Wireframes → Figma (per [[Figma Handoff Notes]] and [[File Storage Rules]])
